 Log in Tigers agree to six-year extension with newly converted starter Troy Melton (source)
 35 minutes ago MLB.com
 Share share-square--:R1qlq: The Tigers have come to an agreement with right-hander Troy Melton on a six-year extension that is expected to be worth $46.5 million, a source told MLB.com's Mark Feinsand. The club has not confirmed the deal.
 The contract includes a club option for 2033 and can be worth as much as $80 million with incentives, per a source.
 Melton was converted to a starting role last season and excelled as a member of the Detroit rotation. He made 20 starts with a 2.76 ERA, 94 strikeouts to 37 walks and a 152 ERA+. That was after he put up a 150 ERA+ in his rookie season spent mostly as a reliever.

 After one blowup inning in the 2025 AL Wild Card Series against the Guardians, Melton bounced back in the Division Series against the Mariners, making three appearances over eight innings, striking out eight and only allowing one run. 
 The 25-year-old Melton, a fourth-round pick by the Tigers in 2022 out of San Diego State, was not yet eligible for arbitration, having just over a year of service time. It's the longest contract for a Detroit pitcher since Justin Verlander's seven-year extension in 2013.
